thread:
Mike (Customer): Hi team — Private deployment collector v2.3.1 failing to upload debug bundle. We get a 400 checksum_mismatch when POSTing the manifest to our presign URL. Happened after a Windows host tried a debug bundle.

Olivia (Support): Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the request id and a minimal curl repro? Also which collector binary (sha) and OS?

Mike (Customer): Request-ID: rq_0c8f2b91. Collector binary: collector-2.3.1+20240207 (sha: a1b2c3d). Host is Windows Server 2019 behind corporate proxy. curl repro below (sanitized):

```
curl -v -X POST "https://presign.example.redwood/signed" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: rq_0c8f2b91" \
  -d @manifest.json
```

Server returns: 400 {"error":"checksum_mismatch","expected":"e3b0c...","got":"e3b0c...0d0a"}

Nikhil (CollectorEng): That looks suspiciously like CRLF conversion (0d0a). Windows tools sometimes convert LF->CRLF when creating tar/streams. Did manifest.json come from a Windows git checkout or created with Notepad?

Mike (Customer): Manifest was created by our support script on the Windows host using PowerShell's Out-File. We did use default encoding.

Olivia (Support): Ok please run the collector debug-gather command with --redact and attach the produced debug bundle. If upload fails, we can do an scp fallback. Command: 

```
collector.exe debug-gather --output C:\tmp\debugbundle.tar.gz --redact --log-level debug
```

Also grab the collector logs around the upload (last 200 lines). You can paste them here or attach.

Mike (Customer): Ran command, upload still fails with 403 when hitting presign, different path this time: auth: invalid_signature. Logs show presign URL includes a query param expiry=60. We see clock skew of ~120s in the logs. Snippet: 

```
[2024-11-08T14:12:03Z] upload: presign request -> signed_url=... expiry=60s
[2024-11-08T14:14:03Z] upload: got 403 invalid_signature (x-request-id: rq_0c8f2b91)
[2024-11-08T14:14:03Z] system: local clock offset +118s
```

Julia (Oncall): That +118s clock skew will cause presign failure if expiry short. Two actions: 1) sync the host clock (w32tm /resync) and 2) re-generate debug bundle with explicit presign extension. Sam, can we extend presign expiry for support flows?

Sam (SRE): We have a temporary backend toggle to bump presign expiry to 10m for support. @olivia if you give me the customer account id I can enable it for 1 hour. But clock sync is preferred.

Mike (Customer): We synced clock, retried, now getting checksum_mismatch again. Full header trace from curl (sanitized):

```
> POST /signed HTTP/1.1
> Host: presign.example.redwood
> User-Agent: curl/7.79.1
> Accept: */*
> Content-Type: application/json
> Content-Length: 842
> X-Request-ID: rq_0c8f2b91
> Date: Fri, 08 Nov 2024 14:15:10 GMT

< HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
< x-request-id: rq_0c8f2b91
< content-type: application/json
< content-length: 123

{"error":"checksum_mismatch","expected":"e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4...","got":"e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e40d0a"}
```

Olivia (Support): Thanks — that confirms CRLF in the payload. For Windows, PowerShell's Out-File uses \r\n by default. Two options: (A) recreate manifest with Unix line endings: `Set-Content -NoNewline` or use `-Encoding ASCII` and `Get-Content -Raw | Out-File -Encoding utf8 -NoNewline`; (B) on collector side, use `--preserve-line-endings` flag (we don't have that in 2.3.1).

Nikhil (CollectorEng): We can add a quick client-side normalization to ignore trailing CR in checksum calculation, but that requires a patch. Meanwhile, a practical repro step we need from you: 1) produce a small manifest file that reproduces checksum mismatch, 2) run `cmd /c type manifest.json | openssl dgst -sha256` on both Windows and WSL to compare, 3) attach the failing manifest + raw debug bundle (unredacted ok) or at minimum the raw manifest (we only need <10KB).

Mike (Customer): Attaching manifest content inline (sanitized):

```
{
  "collector_version": "2.3.1",
  "files": [
    {"path":"C:\\\\ProgramData\\collector\\logs\\app.log","sha256":"e3b0c..."}
  ]
}
```

Olivia (Support): I can repro locally quickly. @Nikhil can you confirm whether server checksum verification trims CRLF? It appears not. If we accept both, risk of accepting tampered files.

Nikhil (CollectorEng): Server expects bytes exact. We'll discuss relaxing acceptance. For now we want: - the raw manifest file; - collector upload log with full curl command for presign; - debug bundle if possible. If upload fails, use scp fallback: `scp C:\tmp\debugbundle.tar.gz support@support-upload.redwood:/incoming/` (we'll provide SSH key).

Olivia (Support): To speed triage I enabled presign expiry extension for customer-account-8821 for 1 hour. Try upload again and, if fails, please either attach the debug bundle to this thread or notify and we'll provide SCP creds.

Mike (Customer): Upload succeeded after clock sync and recreating manifest with LF-only. I attached `manifest-lf.json` and the collector log (snippets). However we still want a patch because our internal pipelines generate manifests on Windows.

Sam (SRE): Filing an internal ticket ENG-RUNTIME-548 to add normalization option or server-side tolerant checksum verification with strict audit trail. @Nikhil please add collector workaround in a patch release.

Nikhil (CollectorEng): Will add a small normalization before checksum in next minor (2.3.2) and include a CLI flag `--normalize-lf` for Windows. I'll also add a test harness for CRLF cases.

Olivia (Support): Closing loop — Mike, thanks for quick repro and logs. If you can, please keep the `manifest-lf.json` sample in case we need to add tests. I'll follow up with the eng ticket link and the scp creds we used (removed after upload). :thumbsup:

Mike (Customer): Thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turnaround! :rocket:
